title: Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Anti-money laundering measures taken
sections.summary: Measures include adopting prevention, detection and enforcement pillars, passing the Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters Act 2024, and supporting global trends against money laundering and financing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The measures which have been taken include: (a) adopting the three key pillars of prevention, detection and enforcement, as set out in the report by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Anti-Money Laundering published recently in October 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For instance, the Government has passed the Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters Act 2024, which will enhance the ability of the Government to detect and act against money laundering with enhanced data sharing and strengthened prosecutorial levers; and (c) supporting global trends to combat money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

sections.label: Freezing property for foreign offences
sections.summary: The Bill lets Singapore help identify, freeze, seize or confiscate property intended to be used in connection with a foreign offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, with this Bill, Singapore can assist to identify, freeze, seize or confiscate property "intended to be used" in connection with the commission of a foreign offence.

sections.label: Enforcing foreign confiscation orders
sections.summary: Singapore will be able to enforce foreign confiscation orders made by a competent authority, in addition to orders made by a Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Fourth, Singapore will be able to enforce foreign confiscation orders made by "a competent authority", in addition to such orders made by a Court.

sections.label: Competent authority orders and extradition
sections.summary: Recognising competent authority confiscation orders helps deprive criminals of proceeds, and the foreign state amendment clarifies extradition requests may be made to any territory.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Recognising confiscation orders made by a "competent authority" will enhance Singapore's ability to deprive criminals of their illicit proceeds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We have updated the amendment of "foreign state" to clarify that it is within Singapore's sovereign power to make an extradition request to any territory and not only those listed in the Third Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For example, the Bill will allow an overseas document to be deemed, to be authenticated under the MACMA or the Extradition Act, when it is sealed with an official or public seal, or stamped with an official stamp of that country, or of a minister, a department or official of the government of that country.

sections.label: Trustees holding trust information
sections.summary: For CDD checks to work and banks to obtain information, trustees must obtain and hold information about the trust they administer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For these CDD checks to work and for the banks to be able to obtain the information needed to prevent money laundering, financing of terrorist and proliferation activities, trustees must be required to obtain and hold information about the trust that they administer.

sections.label: Trustees Act fines and enforcement
sections.summary: Part 7 Trustees Act maximum fine is updated to S$25,000, composition of up to half the fine is introduced, and a Commissioner of Trust Enforcement gains investigation powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To ensure alignment with the maximum fine for other similar offences and that the sanctions for breaches of obligations introduced under Part 7 of the Trustees Act are dissuasive and effective, we will update the maximum fine provided for in Part 7 of the Trustees Act to S$25,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments also introduce the power of composition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Thus, in appropriate cases, a composition sum of up to one-half of the amount of the maximum fine may be levied in lieu of prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The third set of amendments will grant a public officer called the Commissioner of Trust Enforcement (CTE) under the Ministry of Law the power to investigate offences under Part 7 of the Trustees Act.

sections.label: Anti-money laundering trust amendments
sections.summary: The amendments bolster Singapore's anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing and proliferation financing strategy by preventing trust misuse by criminals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Collectively, these amendments will bolster Singapore's national strategy for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism and proliferation financing by preventing trusts from being misused by criminals.

sections.label: Questions on foreign criminal probes
sections.summary: The proposed changes broaden cooperation and permit statements for foreign criminal probes, raising important questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed changes, particularly those broadening cooperation and permitting statements for foreign criminal probes, raise important questions.

sections.label: Financial institutions customer data access
sections.summary: The updated regulations permit financial institutions greater access to customer data, a sensitive matter for many residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The updated regulations permit financial institutions greater access to customer data, which can be a sensitive matter for many residents.

sections.label: Safeguards against foreign confiscation orders
sections.summary: The passage asks what safeguards protect residents from unjust foreign confiscation orders and proposes a cap or stricter criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What safeguards exist to protect residents from unjust foreign confiscation orders?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given that foreign legal standards can vary widely, how can Singaporeans contest potentially unfair seizures based on foreign laws?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also propose implementing a cap or stricter criteria for enforcing foreign confiscation orders.

sections.label: International criminal cooperation framework
sections.summary: The amendments in this Bill aim to bolster Singapore's framework for international cooperation on criminal matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendments in this Bill aim to bolster Singapore's framework for international cooperation on criminal matters.

sections.label: Rising compliance and operational costs
sections.summary: Compliance and operational costs are likely to rise, particularly for financial institutions and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Compliance and operational costs are likely to rise, particularly for financial institutions and businesses.

sections.label: Reciprocity and smaller firms
sections.summary: Amendments need reciprocal commitment from other jurisdictions, and smaller firms with limited compliance resources may struggle, possibly consolidating the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While Singapore is committed to fulfilling international requests for assistance, these amendments will only be effective if there is a reciprocal commitment from other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Smaller firms, particularly those with limited compliance resources, could find it difficult to meet the new standards, leading to a possible consolidation of the market.

sections.label: Trustees Act cost impact
sections.summary: The amendments to the Trustees Act are unlikely to raise financial and operational costs significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The amendments to the Trustees Act are unlikely to raise financial and operational costs significantly.

sections.label: Refusal for non-Singapore offences
sections.summary: A request must be refused if it concerns conduct that would not have constituted a Singapore offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For instance, a request must be refused if it relates to the investigation, prosecution or punishment of a person in respect of any conduct which, if it had occurred in Singapore, would not have constituted a Singapore offence.

sections.label: Minister as further check
sections.summary: Under section 41 of MACMA, the Minister acts as a further check that action is in Singapore's sovereignty, security or public order interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In addition to assessing whether any ground for refusal under section 20 may apply, under section 41 of MACMA, the Minister acts as a further check to ensure that the taking of any action is in the interests of the sovereignty, security or public order of Singapore.

sections.label: Production order requirements
sections.summary: To obtain a production order for financial institution information, the court must be satisfied of reasonable grounds, substantial value, and public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For instance, to obtain a production order for information in the possession of a financial institution, the court must be satisfied that: (a) there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that a person has carried on or benefited from a foreign offence; (b) there are reasonable grounds for believing that the thing is likely to be of substantial value to the criminal matter, and is not subject to legal privilege; and (c) it is not contrary to public interest for the thing to be produced or that access to it be given.

sections.label: Reciprocity undertaking requirement
sections.summary: Based on section 16 of MACMA, the country must give an undertaking of reciprocity and the same safeguards apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Based on section 16 of the MACMA, we will require the country to give an undertaking of reciprocity and the same safeguards in the MACMA will apply to its request.

sections.label: MACMA foreign request undertaking
sections.summary: Under the MACMA, foreign authorities must undertake that requested information or things will not be used for another matter without the Attorney-General's consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Under the MACMA, foreign authorities must undertake that the information or thing requested will not be used for a matter other than the criminal matter in respect of which the request was made, except with the consent of the Attorney‑General.

sections.label: Clause 8 Attorney-General options
sections.summary: Clause 8 of the Bill will give the Attorney-General more options to decide how a thing is handled or disposed of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Clause 8 of the Bill will give the Attorney-General more options to decide how a thing is to be handled or disposed of.

sections.label: Protection from foreign confiscation orders
sections.summary: These protect citizens and residents from unjust foreign confiscation orders, and a cap is not advisable as it might lead to arbitrary results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: These protect our citizens and our residents from any unjust foreign confiscation orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I do not think it would be advisable to introduce a cap on foreign confiscation orders, as this might lead to arbitrary results.
